title: Vector Search
shortDefinition: A similarity search method that retrieves items by comparing embedding vectors rather than exact keywords.
definition: Vector search is a retrieval method that finds similar text, images, audio, or records by comparing their embedding vectors in a mathematical space. Instead of matching exact words, it ranks items by how close their vectors are to the query vector, which makes it a core building block for semantic search, RAG, recommendations, and similarity detection.
introduction: Vector search lets AI systems retrieve information by meaning. Content is converted into embeddings, stored in a vector database or vector-capable index, and searched with nearest-neighbor algorithms so conceptually related items can be found even when they use different wording.

sections.title: How vector search works
sections.description: Vector search compares embeddings to find the nearest semantic matches.

content.text: A vector search system first converts content into embeddings: arrays of numbers that represent semantic meaning. When a user submits a query, the query is embedded the same way and compared against stored vectors using a distance or similarity metric such as cosine similarity, dot product, or Euclidean distance. The closest vectors become the top search results.

items: Embed documents, products, images, or other records.
Store vectors in a vector database or vector-capable index.
Embed the search query at request time.
Rank stored vectors by similarity to the query vector.
Return the matching source records to the application.

content.title: The key insight
content.text: Vector search finds nearby meanings, not just matching words. That is why a query can surface relevant content even when the exact phrase is absent.

Keyword search is excellent for exact terms, names, identifiers, and filters. Vector search is stronger for conceptual discovery, synonyms, natural-language questions, and multimodal retrieval. Production systems often combine both as hybrid search so users get exact-match precision and semantic recall.

faqs.title: Frequently asked questions about vector search

items.question: Is vector search the same as semantic search?
items.answer: Vector search is the technical retrieval method. Semantic search is a user-facing search experience that commonly uses vector search to find results by meaning.

items.question: Do I need a vector database for vector search?
items.answer: For production scale, usually yes. Small prototypes can use in-memory indexes, but production systems need durable storage, indexing, filtering, monitoring, and update workflows.

items.question: Why combine vector search with keyword search?
items.answer: Vector search is strong at conceptual matching, while keyword search is strong at exact terms. Hybrid search combines both so retrieval performs well across more query types.
